answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards, with disputes settled by randomly selected peers who also have stake at risk. If an ivory-market agent on the mesa earns trust through verified deliveries, a raven-like swarm cannot cheaply copy that record: every new identity must fund its own stake, and proven fraud burns it. This raises the attack cost in capital and forfeited value, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker outright.
